## Order physical fills, exchange and corner refresh (`apply_boundaries; exchange_ghost_zones`) {#sec-ch11-timing}

### Summary

Two fillers write ghosts and their footprints overlap at the corners of a block. The physical callbacks own
the ghost slabs of physical faces, the whole orthogonal extent included; the exchange owns the slabs of
layout faces, corners excluded when `skip_corner` is on. A corner slab that lies in a physical x1 face's
ghost region and in a tangential layout face's ghost region is written by the exchange with the neighbour's
column, after which the x1 wall of that column has to be re-imposed. This scheme states the order in which
the two fillers run and the refresh that keeps the overlap consistent.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Order physical fills and exchanged-corner refresh.

**Data.** Hydro state and tracers in their current representation.

**Placement.** Driver order differs between block and mesh stepping.

**Activation.** Automatic with the driver; no independent YAML switch.

**Guarantee / limits.** Refresh requires idempotent callbacks and excludes outflow.

**Evidence.** Report checks and source-test limits are in the Tests layer.
:::

### Derivation

This is an operator-order contract. Copying neighbour values and applying a physical wall need not commute
at their overlap: the exchange overwrites a wall corner with the neighbour's interior column. Re-applying
the wall map to the newly exchanged strip restores the same parity relation as on the owned strip, provided
the callback reads only interior values and is idempotent. The registry contract (`BC_FUNCTION`,
{{< code src/bc/bc_func.hpp BC_FUNCTION >}}) and the `refresh` closure of
`MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}})
encode these requirements. Check C1 includes a two-dimensional corner where an exchange overwrites a prior
mirror and a second fill restricted to the exchanged strip restores parity; this is an exact discrete
ownership check, not a convergence proof [check `src/snapy_report/ch11/checks/boundary_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch11/checks/boundary_check.out`]. The checks do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

Initialization (`MeshBlockImpl::initialize`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize >}})
runs `initialize_local`, which captures the outflow background before any physical fill and then fills the
primitives; exchanges the primitives (and the scalar ratios) with `interpolate` on; and runs
`finalize_initialization`, which converts to conserved variables, records the solid fill states, and fills
the conserved fields. The block driver `MeshBlockImpl::forward`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::forward >}}) exchanges and then advances, so a change the
driver made between calls reaches the ghosts before reconstruction. `MeshImpl::forward`
({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}) advances every local block and then exchanges; with
several local blocks it defers the gravity-work fixer, sums its terms over the blocks, applies the shared
correction, and fills the physical boundaries once more before that exchange. Inside each local advance
(`MeshBlockImpl::advance_local`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}) the order is:
the RK[^rg-882f6e8985e2] combination; the refill of the solid hydro cells; the saturation adjustment on the last stage when a
thermodynamics module is present; the gravity-work fixer on the last stage when it is on and not deferred;
and then the physical fills of `apply_boundaries`.

The refresh in `exchange_ghost_zones` uses only the first two callbacks (x1 inner and outer), skips an
outflow callback, and restricts each call to the tangential ghost slabs whose own face is not physical,
where "physical" here excludes a callback whose name starts with `periodic`. Each slab is $\min(n_g,
\lfloor n/2\rfloor)$ cells wide in the tangential direction, with $n$ that direction's extent. A callback whose name
starts with `reflecting` is instead called once over the full extent when no tangential face is physical: it mirrors
each x1 row from that row's own interior, so the one call writes the slabs and rewrites the other ghost rows with
the values they already hold. The conserved
hydro state and the scalar densities are refreshed, and the scalar primitive ratios are then recomputed from
them. Auxiliary fields take the same two-step order: the donor factor of the flux positivity limiter is
exchanged raw and then passed through every installed callback with scalar type, in `HydroImpl::forward`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) for the species and in the `sync_theta` closure
of `ScalarImpl::forward` ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}) for the passive scalars. No
accuracy order follows from this sequence; the wall-rest and phase-change tests are the available assertions.

### Code

**How to use.** This fragment selects the physical callback, not the schedule. Initialize through the driver and
retain its stage loop. Changes between block `forward` calls reach the next reconstruction through its leading
exchange.

This is a configuration fragment, not a standalone simulation deck.

```yaml
boundary-condition:
  external:
    x1-inner: reflecting
    x1-outer: reflecting
```

**Refusals and prerequisites.** There is no timing YAML switch and no independent schedule validator. The callback
contract forbids dependence on the full tangential extent. Outflow is deliberately excluded from corner refresh
because it needs full-size saved backgrounds.

**Read the implementation.** `MeshBlockImpl::forward` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::forward >}}) contains:

```cpp
exchange_ghost_zones(vars);
advance_local(vars, dt, stage);
```

These lines implement the block-driver ownership order in the Derivation layer. The mesh driver has the different order documented above; this excerpt is not its schedule.

| initlocal | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize_local >}} | `boundary_reference_w` | none |
| finalinit | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finalize_initialization >}} | `fill_solid_hydro_u` | none |
| block | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::forward >}} | `exchange_ghost_zones` | none |
| advance | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}} | `apply_boundaries` | none |

: Implementation sites for timing. {#tbl-ch11-timing-code}

1. Initialize: capture the outflow background, fill the primitives, exchange them, convert, fill the conserved
   fields. The anchor `boundary_reference_w` is in
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize_local >}}.
2. Use the order of the selected driver; the two drivers do not place their exchange at the same point. The
   anchor `advance_local` is in {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}.
3. After a block exchange, refresh the x1 wall corners in the conserved and scalar representations and
   recompute the scalar ratios. The anchor `refresh` is in
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}.
4. At stage end, fill the physical faces after the solid refill, the saturation adjustment and the gravity
   correction. The anchor `apply_boundaries` is in {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Only the x1 callbacks take part in the refresh, and outflow is excluded from it: an outflow x1 face keeps the
exchanged corner, because its background is sized for the full block and it needs primitives. The public
`MeshImpl::exchange_ghost_zones` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}) only builds
the sync options and calls the exchange, so a caller cannot assume it supplies the block method's refresh. A
custom callback that depends on the full orthogonal shape of its input violates the documented contract and
is not refreshed correctly.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result
is claimed.
:::
